title: What did you do yesterday?
goal: Talk about things that have already happened, and understand why the Polish past tense changes with the speaker's gender.
bekal: forming a past-tense sentence from any dictionary form
choosing the masculine, feminine or plural ending correctly
using the most common past time expressions

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Co robiłeś wczoraj?
dialogs.intro: Morning in the canteen. Budi looks short on sleep; Ania is waiting for an explanation.

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.id: What did you do last night?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Byłem w kinie z kolegami. A ty?
lines.id: I went to the cinema with friends. You?
lines.literal: I-was-m in cinema with friends. and you?

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.text: Byłam w domu. Czytałam i wcześnie poszłam spać.
lines.id: I was at home. I read and went to bed early.
lines.literal: I-was-f in home. I-read-f and early I-went-f sleep.

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.text: Dzwoniłam dwa razy, ale nie odbierałeś.
lines.id: I called twice, but you didn't pick up.
lines.literal: I-called-f two times, but not you-picked-up-m.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Przepraszam, telefon był wyciszony w kinie.
lines.id: Sorry, my phone was on silent at the cinema.
lines.literal: sorry, phone was silenced in cinema.

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.id: No problem. How was the film?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Bardzo dobry. Śmialiśmy się przez dwie godziny.
lines.id: Really good. We laughed for two whole hours.
lines.literal: very good. we-laughed self for two hours.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Poszliśmy na piwo. Wróciłem do domu o północy.
lines.id: We went for a beer. I got home at midnight.
lines.literal: we-went for beer. I-returned-m to home at midnight.

lines.speaker: Ania:
lines.id: That's why you look so tired today.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Exactly. But it was worth it.

notes: **Robiłeś or robiłaś?** The Polish past tense **carries the speaker's gender**. Men: *robiłem, robiłeś, robił*. Women: *robiłam, robiłaś, robiła*. English has nothing like this, and it's the only hard part of this unit.
**That means you have to think about who's speaking.** If you're a woman, you say *byłam*; if you're a man, *byłem*. Getting this wrong is the beginner's mistake a Polish ear catches fastest.
**You can still drop the pronoun**, because the ending already marks both the person and the gender. *Byłam w domu* is complete: "(I, a woman) was at home".

**Poszłam, poszliśmy** — the past of *iść* is completely irregular: *poszedłem* (m), *poszłam* (f), *poszliśmy* (we, incl. men), *poszłyśmy* (we, all women). It's too common to skip, so learn all four.
**Śmialiśmy się** — *się* verbs keep their *się* in the past, and it can still move: *śmialiśmy się* or *się śmialiśmy*.
**Przez dwie godziny** — "for two hours". The preposition *przez* says how long something lasted and takes the object form.
**Było warto** — "it was worth it". Subjectless words (*trzeba*, *można*, *warto*) go into the past by adding *było* in front: *trzeba było* (you should have), *można było* (you could have).

grammars.title: Forming the past tense
body: Three steps, no helper words: take the dictionary form, drop *-ć*, add the ending that matches the subject.
after: The "masculine" column is also used for **mixed** groups — one man among ten women is enough for *robiliśmy*. The "feminine" column is for groups made up entirely of women, children or things.
Notice the letter **ł** in every form. That's the real past-tense marker; the ending after it just shows who did it.

Verbs of every group behave the same way in the past: *czytać → czytałem*, *mówić → mówiłem*, *pracować → pracowałem*. After all the complications of the present tense, the past is actually more regular.

grammars.title: Być in the past — and five irregular verbs
body: *Być* is the most used, and the five verbs below have past forms you can't guess from the dictionary form.
after: *Byłem w…* is how you say "I've been to…": *Byłem w Warszawie* — I've been to Warsaw. Polish doesn't need a separate "have been" form.
Negating works as usual — *nie* in front: *Nie byłem w domu*, *Nie widziałam go*. And remember that a negated object moves to *dopełniacz*: *Nie miałem czasu*.

blocks.text: *Temu* always comes **after** the length of time, just like English "ago": *tydzień temu* (a week ago), *pięć minut temu* (five minutes ago).

blocks.title: Asking about the past
items: *Co robiłeś w weekend?* (m) / *Co robiłaś…?* (f) — What did you do on the weekend?
*Gdzie byłeś wczoraj?* — Where were you yesterday?
*Podobało ci się?* — Did you like it?
*Byłeś kiedyś w Polsce?* — Have you ever been to Poland?

blocks.text: Every verb is in the past tense. Read it twice: once slowly while looking at the translation, once a little faster without looking.

head: Polski
English
rows: On Saturday I slept in until eleven.
I had breakfast and walked to the park.
*Pogoda była piękna — słońce i osiemnaście stopni.*
The weather was beautiful — sunshine and eighteen degrees.
I met Ania by the fountain.
*Potem poszliśmy na obiad do małej restauracji.*
Then we had lunch at a small restaurant.
I ordered pierogi, Ania ordered soup.
Everything was delicious and not expensive.

blocks.title: The most useful exercise this week
items: Rewrite the story above with your own details — day, place, food, friends. Ten sentences, no more.
If you're a woman, change every *-łem* ending to *-łam*, and *-szedłem* to *-szłam*. Doing this once, consciously, locks in the rule better than reading the table ten times.
Read the result aloud. Any sentence you stumble over is the one to repeat tomorrow.
